title: An Honest Word About the Future

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he will live in hostility toward all his brothers." - Gen 16:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's word about Ishmael's future is strikingly honest - even hard. His life would be marked by conflict and independence, "a wild donkey of a man," free and untamed, often at odds with those around him. This was not the smooth, easy future a mother might dream of for her son. God tells Hagar the truth, not a comforting fiction.

There is something we can learn from God's honesty here. He does not flatter Hagar with false promises about a trouble-free life. He gives her a true picture, hard as it is. God's love is never sentimental; it deals in reality. He would rather tell us the truth than soothe us with lies.

Yet even in this hard word, notice the mercy. Ishmael would live - he would survive, grow strong, and become a people. God was giving Hagar real information to live by, and a future for her son, difficult though it would be.

We often want God to promise us an easy road. But God's honesty is better than false comfort. He tells us the truth about a fallen world where conflict is real, and He walks with us through it. Jesus was equally honest: "In this world you will have trouble." But He didn't stop there - "take heart! I have overcome the world" (John 16:33). God gives us truth we can build on, not illusions that will collapse.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you prefer God's honest truth or comforting illusions?
- How does God's realism about a fallen world actually help you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You tell me the truth rather than soothing me with illusions. Help me build my life on Your honest word about this world, and take heart that in Christ You have overcome it.
Amen.
